extracted.intended_audience: USPTO examiners, international-stage patent applicants/agents, and patent practitioners handling PCT international searches and U.S. national-stage entries
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for determining whether an international (PCT) application satisfies the requirement of unity of invention before an International Searching Authority (and related U.S. national-stage practice), and the procedures for invitations to pay additional fees, payment under protest, and notifications. Covers special situations (combinations of claim categories, Markush groupings, intermediate/final products, nucleotide sequences) and administrative/form procedures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Requirement of unity of invention (PCT Rule 13.1)
rubrics_metrics.description: The international application shall relate to one invention only or to a group of inventions so linked as to form a single general inventive concept ('requirement of unity of invention').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is the foundational standard applied by the International Searching Authority (ISA) and is relevant during international and national stages. The concept of a 'single general inventive concept' is applied by examining whether claimed inventions are linked by special technical features that define a contribution over the prior art.

rubrics_metrics.name: When unity is fulfilled (PCT Rule 13.2: special technical features)
rubrics_metrics.description: Unity is fulfilled only when there is a technical relationship among those inventions involving one or more of the same or corresponding special technical features. 'Special technical features' means those technical features that define a contribution which each of the claimed inventions, considered as a whole, makes over the prior art.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Determination is made on the contents of the claims interpreted in light of the description and drawings. Whether a technical feature is 'special' must be considered with respect to novelty and inventive step. The standard can be applied a priori or a posteriori depending on prior-art findings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Determination not affected by manner of claiming (PCT Rule 13.3 / 37 CFR 1.475(e))
rubrics_metrics.description: The determination whether a group of inventions forms a single general inventive concept shall be made without regard to whether the inventions are claimed in separate claims or as alternatives within a single claim.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Objections can arise within a single claim if it contains distinct embodiments that are not linked by a single general inventive concept. Conversely, merely claiming alternatives within a single claim does not prevent a unity determination; the substance governs, not claim drafting form.

rubrics_metrics.name: Dependent claims allowance (PCT Rule 13.4)
rubrics_metrics.description: Subject to Rule 13.1, it is permitted to include in the same international application a reasonable number of dependent claims, claiming specific forms of the invention claimed in an independent claim, even where the features of any dependent claim could be considered as constituting in themselves an invention.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the independent claim avoids the prior art and satisfies unity, dependent claims do not typically give rise to a lack-of-unity objection even if a dependent claim contains a further patentable invention (examples provided).

rubrics_metrics.name: Utility model national-law exception (PCT Rule 13.5)
rubrics_metrics.description: Any designated State in which the grant of a utility model is sought on the basis of an international application may apply its national law concerning utility models in place of Rules 13.1–13.4 once processing has started in that State, provided the applicant has at least two months to adapt the application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applies on a per-designated-State basis; applicants must be allowed time to adapt to national utility-model requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: ISA invitation to pay additional fees and time limit (PCT Rule 40.1)
rubrics_metrics.description: The invitation to pay additional fees shall: (i) specify reasons why the application is not considered to comply with unity; (ii) invite the applicant to pay additional fees within one month and indicate amounts; and (iii) invite payment of any protest fee within one month and indicate amount.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The invitation must be specific about grounds and fees; timing requirements are strict and start the applicant's window to act.

rubrics_metrics.name: Additional fees and protest rights (PCT Rule 40.2)
rubrics_metrics.description: The amount of additional fees is determined by the ISA and payable directly to it. Any applicant may pay additional fees under protest, accompanied by a reasoned statement arguing unity or excessive fees. A review body examines the protest and may order reimbursement if justified; a protest fee may be required and refundable if protest entirely justified.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Protests are examined by a review body that may include the original decision-maker; applicants should submit reasoned statements and may request that protest texts and decisions be forwarded to designated Offices with translations as appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: U.S. regulatory statement of unity (37 CFR 1.475)
rubrics_metrics.description: An international and national-stage application shall relate to one invention only or to a group of inventions so linked as to form a single general inventive concept. Unity exists only when there is a technical relationship among inventions involving one or more of the same or corresponding special technical features.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Mimics PCT Rule 13.1–13.2 and is the US-specific codification used by USPTO examiners when acting as ISA/IPEA or processing national-stage entries.

rubrics_metrics.name: Permissible combinations of claim categories (37 CFR 1.475(b) / MPEP list)
rubrics_metrics.description: An application containing claims to different categories of invention will be considered to have unity if the claims are drawn only to certain combinations (e.g., product + process specially adapted to manufacture product; product + process of use; process + apparatus specifically designed to carry it out; product + process + apparatus combinations).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The emphasis differs per combination: (A)/(C) emphasize the product, (B) emphasizes the process. The 'specially adapted' and 'specifically designed' language requires corresponding contributions over the prior art (see detailed guidance).

rubrics_metrics.name: Interpretation of 'specially adapted' and 'specifically designed' in category combinations
rubrics_metrics.description: A process is 'specially adapted' for manufacture if it inherently results in the product; an apparatus is 'specifically designed' if its contribution over prior art corresponds to that of the process.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: 'Specially adapted' does not mean the product couldn't be made by another process; 'specifically designed' does not mean the apparatus couldn't be used for other processes—what matters is the correspondence of contributions over prior art.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid raising or maintaining unity objections on narrow or academic grounds
rubrics_metrics.description: Lack of unity should not be raised or maintained on the basis of a narrow, literal or academic approach; there should be a broad, practical consideration of the degree of interdependence of alternatives in relation to the state of the art, with benefit of doubt given to the applicant.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examiners should consider the interdependence revealed by the international search and additional documents, and avoid overly strict parsing that would unfairly split inventions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Don't object solely because of classification differences
rubrics_metrics.description: The ISA/IPEA should not raise lack of unity merely because inventions are classified in separate classification groups or to restrict the search to certain classification groups.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Classification differences alone are insufficient grounds for lack-of-unity objections; substantive technical linkage is required.

rubrics_metrics.name: Unity primarily considered in relation to independent claims
rubrics_metrics.description: Unity of invention is considered in the first place only in relation to independent claims, not the dependent claims. A dependent claim contains all features of one or more other claims and additional features.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Even if a dependent claim contains an independent invention, no objection under PCT Rule 13 arises if the independent claim avoids the prior art and satisfies unity. Definitions per PCT Rule 6.4 apply.

rubrics_metrics.name: A posteriori unity after prior-art assessment
rubrics_metrics.description: If an independent claim does not avoid the prior art, the question whether there remains an inventive link between dependent claims must be carefully considered; lack of unity may be raised a posteriori (after assessment of prior art).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If a feature common to claims is known, it may remove the technical link and lead to separate inventions lacking a single general inventive concept.

rubrics_metrics.name: Initial unity determination and reconsideration after search
rubrics_metrics.description: The method for determining unity is intended to be applied even before the commencement of the international search; where a search is made, an initial determination (assuming claims avoid the prior art) may be reconsidered based on search results.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examiners should make an initial practical assessment but must be prepared to alter unity findings when prior art shows common matter is known.

rubrics_metrics.name: Unity objections within single claims and alternatives
rubrics_metrics.description: Alternative embodiments contained within a single claim may give rise to lack of unity if the claim contains distinct embodiments not linked by a single general inventive concept.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: PCT Rule 13.3 does not prevent objecting to alternatives in a single claim on grounds of clarity, conciseness, or fee considerations; examiners should watch for distinct unlinked embodiments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Combination of numerous independent claim sets across categories accepted only exceptionally
rubrics_metrics.description: While a single set of independent claims according to permitted category-combinations is permissible, the ISA is not required to accept a proliferation of such sets (e.g., multiple independent claims across product/process/use/apparatus) except exceptionally.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examiners should guard against claim proliferation that multiplies independent sets across categories unless a single general inventive concept clearly links them.

rubrics_metrics.name: Objection does not normally arise for compositionally unrelated combined elements in one claim
rubrics_metrics.description: An objection of lack of unity does not normally arise if the combination of a number of individual elements is claimed in a single claim (as opposed to distinct embodiments).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Single-claim combinations are acceptable even if the elements individually seem unrelated, provided the overall claimed combination has unity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Markush practice — criteria for chemical alternatives to be of 'similar nature'
rubrics_metrics.description: For Markush (alternatives) groupings, the requirement of technical interrelationship and same or corresponding special technical features is met when the alternatives are of a similar nature. For chemical alternatives, this means: (A) all alternatives have a common property or activity; and (B) either (1) a common significant structural element is present, or (2) all alternatives belong to a recognized class of chemical compounds in the art.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Significant structural element means a large or structurally distinctive shared portion in view of prior art. A 'recognized class' implies expectation that members behave similarly and are substitutable with expected same result. If at least one Markush alternative is not novel, reconsider unity; reconsideration does not necessarily require objection.

rubrics_metrics.name: Handling Markush groupings when common structural element not significant
rubrics_metrics.description: If alternatives share a common structure that is not a significant structural element (small or not distinctive in view of prior art) and the alternatives do not belong to a recognized class, they are not regarded as being of similar nature.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examiner should cite prior art demonstrating the common structure is not distinctive and explain why the compounds do not form a recognized class; may result in lack-of-unity finding between groups.

rubrics_metrics.name: Treatment when Markush alternatives lack common structure or recognized class
rubrics_metrics.description: If the chemical compounds of a Markush group do not share a common structure and do not belong to a recognized class, they are not regarded as being of similar nature and unity is not present.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examiner must provide reasoned explanation and identify affected groups/species in the Office action using form paragraphs and bracketed explanatory text.

rubrics_metrics.name: Intermediate and final products unity criteria
rubrics_metrics.description: Unity exists for intermediate and final products where: (A) the intermediate and final products have the same essential structural element (basic chemical structures are the same or technically closely interrelated), and (B) the intermediate and final products are technically interrelated (final product manufactured directly from intermediate or separated by a small number of steps).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The term 'intermediate' includes starting products that are transformed into final products. Both structural and technical interrelationship must be present to sustain unity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Examples and further guidance referenced (International Search & Preliminary Examination Guidelines, Chapter 10)
rubrics_metrics.description: Chapter 10 of the International Search and Preliminary Examination Guidelines contains examples concerning unity of invention (combinations, Markush practice, intermediate/final products).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examiners and practitioners are directed to consult Chapter 10 (via Patent Examiner’s Toolkit or WIPO website) for illustrative examples supporting unity determinations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Protest procedure — transmittal of protest and decision (PCT Administrative Instructions Sec. 502)
rubrics_metrics.description: The ISA shall transmit to the applicant any decision taken under Rule 40.2(c) on the protest against payment of additional fees, preferably together with the international search report, and shall transmit copies of both protest and decision to the International Bureau; applicant may request that texts be forwarded to designated Offices.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Timely transmittal ensures designated Offices see protest context; applicant may request forwarding when filing or before ISR issuance, and must provide translations when required.

rubrics_metrics.name: U.S. protest process (37 CFR 1.477) — pay under protest and Director review
rubrics_metrics.description: If the applicant disagrees with lack-of-unity holding, additional fees may be paid under protest with a statement of reasons and/or request for refund. Protest is examined by the Director or designee; if protest is justified, additional fees or a portion are refunded. Applicant may notify ISA to include protest and decision with the international search report.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For U.S. ISA decisions, protests are decided by a Technology Center Director; payment of additional fees is required for protest to be considered (no protest fee for ISA/US). If applicant wants protest text transmitted with ISR, notify ISA in time or contact International Bureau later.

rubrics_metrics.name: Notification of decision on protest (Form PCT/ISA/212) and signature authority
rubrics_metrics.description: A Notification of Decision of Protest (Form PCT/ISA/212) is used to inform the applicant of the decision; if the protest is found unjustified, a clear concise explanation must be given. Form must be signed by a TC Director.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Space on the form is limited; supplemental attachments should be used when necessary. The form and signature identify the authorized officer deciding protest.

rubrics_metrics.name: Unity of invention — nucleotide sequences exception
rubrics_metrics.description: Nucleotide sequences encoding the same protein are considered to satisfy the unity of invention standard and will continue to be examined together.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Biotechnological inventions with sequences encoding the same protein are treated as unified for search/examination; further biotechnological examples are in Chapter 10 of the Guidelines.

rubrics_metrics.name: Examiners should give benefit of doubt to applicant and apply case-by-case assessment
rubrics_metrics.description: Rigid rules cannot be given for all situations; each case should be considered on its merits, with the benefit of any doubt given to the applicant.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This general principle guides discretionary judgment where unity is borderline; examiners should explain reasoning where they maintain lack-of-unity objections.

rubrics_metrics.name: Form-paragraph and office-action drafting instructions for unity findings
rubrics_metrics.description: The MPEP provides sample examiner form paragraphs for various lack-of-unity scenarios (e.g., alternatives sharing common structure but not significant, alternatives not sharing common structure, identification of groups/species), with examiner notes on how to fill bracketed items.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examiners should use the provided form paragraphs and examiner notes to properly identify groups/species, cite prior art, and explain reasoning; brackets indicate where to insert case-specific details and citations.
